ErrorCode.description: The stable code of a failure, the same in the Rust API and the event stream (`error.code`).

oneOf.description:
The folder isn't a project Isothrum runs: it holds no Compose file, Vagrantfile or
Terraform module, or the files of several formats with none named.

The manifest needs something this runner doesn't do (a target that doesn't run on this
host, a delivery its driver doesn't take, an action of another driver's, a step with no
command for this host), or the call asks the run for something its target can't do (a
console into a Compose service with no VM, a Vagrant VM joined to another network).
A file or folder couldn't be read or written, or a socket on this computer bound.
Another process runs an operation on this run, or holds the home's slot pick.
A tool a step runs isn't installed.
A step's tool ran and failed.

A tool the run needs is installed, but got no answer from its service: Docker's engine
stopped, or quit while a step ran (the `step` says which): the message says what the tool
said.
A tool answers at a version older than the run needs.

A tool refused this account (Docker's engine its socket or named pipe): the account needs
the access (a group), not the tool started.

A cloud refused the sign-in the run's tools use: a CLI or SSO session that ran out, an
expired token, application-default credentials gone stale, a profile never signed in.
Signing in again fixes it; the cloud refused before Terraform changed anything.

A network the run makes needs an address block another network on the engine already
holds (Docker's `Pool overlaps with other one on this address space`).

A step showed no progress for its time limit, or ran to the ceiling every step stops at,
and was stopped, with what it started (the `error` event's `detail` says which).

A download (what a step needs, fetched in a phase of its own before it: a Compose start's
images, a Vagrant start's boxes; or a step the manifest marks a download) showed no
progress for as long as a download may, and was stopped.

A download couldn't be made: its tool failed (the message says why: a registry or a box
catalog refusing it, a name it doesn't know, the network). A failure for the network that
passes (a connection reset, refused or timed out, a gateway's 502, 503 or 504) was tried
again first, up to three more times: the message is the last try's.
The run is already up.
The run is recorded on another place (server or account) than the one asked for.
A host port the run publishes is taken.
The manifest has no park steps for that mode.
Nothing of the run, or not every one of its machines, is left to resume.
The run isn't up.
A ready condition didn't hold.
A required secret or input has no value.

A value or secret that can't be handed to the tools (its name empty or holding `=`, a
NUL in it).
A run name that can't name a run.

The run's Vagrant provider is missing, unknown, not on this host, refused by the run, or
lacks its plugin, or the hypervisor lacks what it needs on this computer (virtiofsd, for a
shared folder on Linux: the `detail`'s `need`).

The elevation Hyper-V's commands need couldn't be had or was lost: the permission prompt
declined or unanswered, the elevated session not started or ended before the operation
(the message says which).
A machine the run doesn't have.
The run has several machines the call could mean, and it named none.
A network the run doesn't have.
A deployment can't be taken over as a run.

The operation was cut short before it ended (its future dropped: an embedder's cancel, the
command line's Ctrl-C or SIGTERM); the tools it started were asked to stop, and are ended
once they have, or 30 seconds later.

The embedder was asked for something that makes no sense (the command line: a run folder
with no manifest, a value missing or malformed), so no operation started.

The machine has no graphical console to reach: its target or provider gives none (the
error says why), it isn't running, or its hypervisor doesn't say where it is.

The server the run is on (Proxmox VE, ESXi) refused the run's credentials: its API
answered 401 or 403, or its tool said the sign-in failed (an API token revoked, a password
changed).

A file of the runner's own (a record, a ledger entry) is there but isn't what it wrote:
not JSON, or another version's shape.

The run's state machine has no such move (a park of a parked run, a resume of a ready
one), or a resource row can't move that way.
The run moved between the read and the write that would have moved it: try again.
The home's store was written by a newer runner.
The home's store isn't a database this runner reads, or holds what it doesn't write.
A live process holds the lease asked for.
A host port the run publishes is taken.

ErrorReport.description:
A failure, as one value: its stable code, its message, the step it happened in, its typed
fields, and whether the run was touched. An embedder branches on [`ErrorReport::code`] and
reads [`ErrorReport::detail`]'s fields; it never needs the runner's [`Error`] variants.

changed.description:
Whether the run may have changed: false only when the failure is a refusal made before
anything acted on the run (another operation holds it, it is already up or isn't up, a
value it needs is missing or unusable, a tool it needs is missing), so whatever the caller
prepared for the operation can be put back. Read as true when absent.

detail.description: The failure's typed fields, when it has any.

message.description: The message: plain and technical, secrets masked.

step.description: The step that failed, when one did.

Event.description:
One event of the stream.

Every event of an operation has `run` and `op`. An event written outside one ([`Event::new`])
has those its writer knows. The command line's own: a command line it refused has neither;
`reap`'s closing `result` and `error` have neither; any other failure before an operation
began has `op` when the command is an operation, and `run` when `--name` named it (a failure
of `status`, `console`, `events` or `key` has no `op`).

oneOf.description: The run moved from one state to another.
A step started, finished, failed or was skipped.

note.description: What it does, said when it starts.

oneOf.description: A line a step's tool printed.

line.description: The line, without its line break.

oneOf.description: An output's value, once the run is up.

value.description: Its value (`***` when sensitive), or null when it can't be read.

oneOf.description: Something the embedder may show, that didn't fail the operation.
The operation's outcome, when it ran to its end.

data.description: What it found or produced, by operation.

ok.description: Whether it reached its goal (false: a check failed).

oneOf.description:
A journaled operation was queued, started or ended: what a runner service says of the
operations it queues (the runner's own operation stream doesn't carry it: it still ends
with exactly one `result` or `error`).

position.description: Its place in its run's queue (0: next), when `phase` is `queued`.

oneOf.description:
What the user wants of the run changed: an operation that moves it began (`up`, `resume`:
running; `park`: parked; `down`: gone).

A resource of the run moved in the home's write-ahead ledger: written `creating` before
the call that makes it, `created` with the tool's id after it, `destroying` before the call
that removes it, `gone` after.

key.description: The resource's key in the run (`container:web-1`, a volume's name, a local thing's kind).

native_id.description: The tool's id for it, once it has one.

oneOf.description:
Why the operation failed: its code, message, step, typed fields and whether the run was
touched ([`crate::ErrorReport`]).

op.description:
The operation: on every event of an operation; outside one, when its writer knows it (see
[`Event`]).

operation.description: The operation's id in the home's journal: on every event of a journaled operation.

run.description:
The run's name: on every event of an operation; outside one, when its writer knows it
(see [`Event`]).

seq.description: Its place in the operation, from 1.

oneOf.description: Running.
Running, but failing its health check.
Exited with this code (a job that finished, or a machine that died).

Not there.
Something else, as the engine says it.

Not read: another process acts on it (Vagrant's lock on the machine, held by a `vagrant

MachineStatus.description: One machine of the run, as its tool reports it.

address.description:
The address it is reached at itself, when its tool says one another computer reaches (a
VM on a bridged or host-only network, a server's VM, a cloud instance); none for one
reached only through its published ports. On ESXi, which forwards no port to this
computer, a machine's ports answer at this address.

console.description:
Its graphical console, as its hypervisor offers it; none for a machine with no screen to
speak of (a container), and while not [`Status::live`].

name.description: Its name in the project (a Compose service, a Vagrant machine, a module's VM).

NativeApp.description:
The hypervisor's own app that shows a running VM's screen in a window of its own, and what of
it this computer must have (any one of `needs`).

name.description: Its name as its maker writes it (`VirtualBox`, `VMware Fusion`): what a button names.

needs.description:
What opens it, best first: the program or app [`NativeConsole::ways`] runs, in the same
order.

NativeApps.description: `screen --app --json`: what opens a machine in its hypervisor's own app.

ways.description:
The ways to open it, best first: the first whose program or app this computer has is the
one to take.

NativeNeed.description: What of a hypervisor's app must be on this computer for a way to open it.

Hot-remove the on-demand access machine from the running run.
Bring the running run up to date with its manifest.

An output's value (a Terraform module's output). A sensitive one shows as `***` wherever it
is written out (its JSON, its `Debug`, an event); the runner keeps the value itself for the
embedder ([`OutputValue::revealed`]).

value.description: Its value, when it can be read; `***` when it is sensitive.

Screen.description: `screen --json`: where a machine's graphical console answers.

address.description:
Where a VNC or RDP viewer connects, on this computer's loopback (`127.0.0.1:5901`); null
for a console reached through its websocket.

note.description: What else to know to connect.

tunnel.description: The machine an SSH tunnel to the console goes through, open while the command runs.

user.description: Who to sign in as, when the console asks.

websocket.description: Proxmox VE's VNC websocket; its ticket is hidden unless `--show-password`.

ShellCommand.description:
The command that opens an interactive console into a machine (a shell in a container, `vagrant
ssh`, an SSH login): the runner builds it (it alone knows the runtime: the Compose project and
files, the Vagrant define, the address and user a module gives), the embedder runs it in its
own terminal. Addresses the machine by service or define name, or by the address the run gives
it, never a guessed container.

cwd.description: The folder to run it in (the run's folder).

env.description:
Variables to run it with, besides the embedder's own (a Vagrant run's state folder,
`VAGRANT_DOTFILE_PATH`, without which Vagrant doesn't find the VM; its forwarded ports).
Empty for a Compose service on this computer and for an SSH login.

ShownOutput.description: An output as a `result` event shows it.

value.description: Its value, when it can be read; `***` when it is sensitive.

desired.description:
What the user wants of the run (the last operation that set it: `up`, `park`, `down`);
none for a run never recorded. With `state`, whether the run is where it should be.

failed_cause.description: Why the run failed, when its recorded state is `failed`.

live.description:
Whether the machines and outputs were read from the engine now. False while an operation
holds the run (in this process or another), whose tools a read would contend with (Vagrant
refuses to read a VM's state while a `vagrant up` provisions it): they are then as the
runner last read them (none before it ever did), and the outputs the engine itself gives
are left out.

native.description:
The hypervisor's own app the run's VMs open in ([`crate::Running::native_console`]); none
where there is none (containers, QEMU), and while not [`Status::live`].

outputs.description:
What the project gives back (a module's outputs), as read; none while not
[`Status::live`].

provider.description: The Vagrant provider it uses, when it has one.

state.description:
Where it stands. While an operation holds the run: the moving state it is in (`creating`
through an `up`), else, before it records one or for an operation that leaves the run as
it was meanwhile (an `update`: `ready`), the state the run's record holds.

oneOf.description: Started.
Finished and succeeded.
Finished and failed (an `error` follows unless the step's failure is tolerated).
Not run: an earlier step failed.

Stream.description: Which output of a tool a line came from.

oneOf.description: Its standard output.
Its standard error.

TimedOut.description:
Which limit a step ran into: a timeout's, also the `error` event's `timeout`.

A step's limit (its `timeout_s`) counts the time it shows no progress: progress is an output
line, on either stream, that isn't blank and isn't one of the last distinct lines it printed
(a stuck download repeating `Downloading 1.121GB` makes none). A step that prints nothing has
its limit from its start. A step that keeps making progress still stops at a ceiling: six
hours from its start, or its limit when that is longer.

oneOf.description: It showed no progress for its limit.

last_line.description:
The last line it printed (secrets masked, cut to 300 bytes); none when it printed
nothing.

oneOf.description:
It was still running at the ceiling: a step still making progress, or a tool call at its
deadline (a command in a machine that never returned).

after_s.description: The ceiling, in seconds from the step's start.

last_line.description:
The last line it printed (secrets masked, cut to 300 bytes); none when it printed
nothing, or when it isn't said.

WarningCode.description: What kind of warning a `warning` event is, the same in the Rust API and the event stream.

oneOf.description: A step whose failure the manifest tolerates failed.
A check runner failed or ran out of time: its checks that didn't report fail.

A clean-up of the checks failed: a check runner's that ran out of time (`on_timeout`), or
the teardown after a setup that failed too (the check ends with the setup's error).
What an earlier run left is removed before a start.
A VM (or its folder) an earlier run left was removed.
The run last ran on another Vagrant provider: that run is cleared first.
A VM's saved state was cut off: it boots fresh.
A start failed on stale state: cleared, then started again.

A step is tried again: an apply that failed, an `ssh.run` whose host doesn't answer yet, a
Vagrant command another Vagrant process's lock on a machine refused, a UTM `up` an Apple
event failed in passing (once), or a download the network cut (a connection reset, a
gateway's 502), up to three more times.

An operation that failed couldn't update the run's record either: the operation's own
error is the one it ends with.

An output's `format` couldn't be filled (it names a value the run doesn't have): the
output has no value.

A resource a destroy found already gone (its provider's error, which the manifest names) is
dropped from the run's state, and the destroy runs again.

A clean-up the runner does on its own, best effort, failed (an earlier run's VM or its
folder, the hypervisor's list of them, the run on another Vagrant provider): what it would have removed may still be
there, and the start goes on.

A Terraform module keeps its state in a backend of its own: every copy of it shares that
state.

A running machine's forwarded ports couldn't be read (its provider can't list them, and
its hypervisor didn't say): it has no published port, and runs on.

A machine's published host port is another than the one the run kept from its first
start (a Vagrant provider's `auto_correct` re-picked it at a boot): its address moved.
A tool printed no version the runner reads: it is used, its minimum version unchecked.

anyOf.description: Run `program` with `args`, each passed as it is.

Way.description: One way to open the app, never through a shell.

description:
What `isothrum <command> --json` prints on standard output, one JSON document per line. Read one line at a time; ignore a field or an event kind you don't know.

- `Event`: Each line of an operation (`up`, `down`, `park`, `resume`, `update`, `retire`, `exec`, `provision`, `attach`, `reap`), of `events`, and any failure.

- `Status`: `status`.

- `ShellCommand`: `console`.

- `Screen`: `screen`.

- `NativeApps`: `screen --app`.

- `PublicKey`: `key`.
